subject: general
question: Two trains are moving in opposite directions at speeds of 110 km/hr and 150 km/hr. The length of one train is 500 m. The time taken by them to cross each other is 10 seconds. The length (in m) of the other train, correct to 2 decimal places, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative Speed (opposite) = 110 + 150 = 260 km/hr

Relative Speed in m/s = 260 × 5/18 = 72.222 m/s

Total Distance (Length sum) = 72.222 × 10 = 722.22 m

Length of other train = 722.22 − 500 = 222.22 m

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of train 1 (S₁) = 110 km/hr

Speed of train 2 (S₂) = 150 km/hr

Length of train 1 (L₁) = 500 m

Time taken (t) = 10 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂
